title: Every gate leaves a machine-readable JSON report at a stable path
asA: downstream reader of the pipeline (a reviewer, a dashboard, an audit tool)
iWant: each gate the suite runs to write a JSON report file at a stable relative path with a stable schema
soThat: I can pick up the gate's outcome without re-running it or scraping the CI provider's log surface

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every gate the suite runs writes a JSON report file at `<reportDir>/<gate>.json` whether the gate passed or failed. The report carries a fixed set of fields: `gate`, `command`, `toolVersion`, `startedAt`, `endedAt`, `durationMs`, `exitCode`, `outcome`, `stdout`, `stderr`.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the suite has run against any tree
acceptanceCriteria.when: the reviewer inspects the configured report directory after the run
acceptanceCriteria.then: for every gate named in the aggregate report's `gates[]` array, a file at `<reportDir>/<gate>.json` exists whose top-level keys are exactly the fixed set above, and the value types match the stable schema (`startedAt` and `endedAt` are ISO-8601 strings, `durationMs` is an integer, `exitCode` is an integer, `outcome` is one of `passed` or `failed`)

acceptanceCriteria.description: The `toolVersion` field records the underlying CLI's version string (the value `rcf --version` prints) at the time the gate ran. A tool-version mismatch across two pipeline runs of the same commit is visible in the report without re-running the gate.
acceptanceCriteria.given: two invocations of the suite against the same commit under two different installed versions of the `rcf` CLI
acceptanceCriteria.when: the reviewer diffs the two runs' per-gate reports
acceptanceCriteria.then: the `toolVersion` field in the affected per-gate reports differs between the two runs, and the value on each side matches what the invoked `rcf --version` prints on that host
